rv.q: All in all, this is a too-rare 22-carat demonstration of silliness as one of the great English virtues.
But it's an evening that reveals more of Wodehouse's gift for farce than of his matchless verbal felicity.
Together with Mark Hadfield, they all turn in an evening full of invention, wit and brilliant characterisation that has to be one of the best and most absurd nights out in London.

Perfect Nonsense is a brilliant farce, which takes Wodehouse's genius for getting his characters into the most improbable and complicated plot tangles and translates it into a well-oiled show bursting with physical comedy.
Perfect Nonsense is hugely successful for offering audiences a night of pure, unbridled entertainment at the theatre, with no airs or pretentions about it.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive Wodehouse adaptation for its physical comedy and charming performances, though some find the framing device effortful. The cast earns raves for brilliant comic timing and characterization.
